answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by requiring every participant to forge a bonded commitment whose value creates a positive economic delta against free identity creation. Attackers must lock scarce capital for each fake agent; the network then measures the delta between claimed stake and verifiable activity. Low-delta forgeries are rejected, so multiplying identities multiplies the capital cost linearly while honest agents amortize one bond across many interactions. This concrete cost barrier, rather than any sonnet of empty promises, enforces genuine participation.
